jobs.description:
Position Purpose: Ensure Corporate & External Affairs liaison with commercial and site leadership in Switzerland. Provide strategic guidance and direction to the affiliate and site leadership teams on government relations, policy, and advocacy, enable early identification and mitigation of policy risks, and leveraging opportunities in support of our operations and commercial priorities. Lead engagement with government in support of site operations and commercial priorities, develop a long-term external engagement plan for the company.
This role reports to:

• International Head Policy, Advocacy and Government Affairs

• Commercial Affiliate and Site Management (dotted line)

Main Responsibilities and Accountabilities:

• Develop and lead execution of strategic plan to drive public affairs, executive though leadership engagement that enable the success of CSL’s operations, business and patient access to our therapies in Switzerland.

• Lead and coordinate CSL company engagement with government officials, industry associations, patient advocacy groups and other stakeholders. Represents CSL and takes leading role in key industry associations and committees. Partners with CSL functions to support external engagement priorities in Switzerland. Partners with Communications team for advancing strategic media relations in Switzerland.

• Lead the development of business-relevant policy updates to senior company leaders, in alignment with relevant affiliate functions and the CEA leadership.

• Serve on Switzerland Commercial Leadership Team, partner and pro-actively collaborate with functional leads, including Therapeutic Areas Commercial, Medical, Market Access, and Regulatory, to develop and execute joint strategies.

• Serve on Bern Site Leadership Team.] Drives strategic site engagement at political level, in partnership with leadership of the manufacturing sites and the communications team.

• Bring strategic insights to shape CEA strategy in Switzerland and International region.

• Is a key interface partner and relationship manager with patient advocacy groups, and works closely with Medical Affairs and Communications teams on patient group engagement and corporate communications strategies and programs in Switzerland.

Position Qualifications and Experience Requirements:
Education:

• Graduate/professional degree in law, public health, international relations, political sciences or similar disciplines preferred.

Experience in Switzerland:

• Minimum 8 years of experience in healthcare policy/public affairs, access or comparable fields

• Experience designing and leading efforts to build company profile and impact with important healthcare public affairs stakeholders at the national and local levels

• Experience collaborating with colleagues at multiple levels of the organization (matrix) to align on and execute shared goals

• Strong understanding of the workings of major government/public authorities and healthcare industry associations

• Experience partnering with patient groups to advance shared policy goals

• Strong, proved network of relationships with government officials, policy makers, industry, patient advocacy, and other stakeholders that are influential in policy formulation

• Experience in biologics, plasma, or pharma products industries preferred

• Experience in media relations or integrated communications campaigns preferred

Competencies :

• Strong analytical skills, including ability to spot risks and draw connections between complex policy issues and business impact

• Strong communications skills, including ability to communicate accurate, succinct descriptions of policy/political developments to senior business and international leaders

• Results oriented & growth mindset

• Strong team player skills and ability to work in a matrix organization and orchestrate cross-functional efforts with tangible results.

• German and English fluency required. Other languages will be an asset.

About CSL Behring
CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients’ needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.

CSL Behring operates one of the world’s largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries.
To learn more about CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor visit https://www.csl.com/ and CSL Plasma at https://www.cslplasma.com/ .

Our Benefits
For more information on CSL benefits visit How CSL Supports Your Well-being | CSL .

You Belong at CSL
At CSL, Inclusion and Belonging is at the core of our mission and who we are. It fuels our innovation day in and day out. By celebrating our differences and creating a culture of curiosity and empathy, we are able to better understand and connect with our patients and donors, foster strong relationships with our stakeholders, and sustain a diverse workforce that will move our company and industry into the future.
To learn more about inclusion and belonging visit https://www.csl.com/careers/inclusion-and-belonging

CSL is an Equal Opportunity Employer. If you are an individual with a disability and need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application process, please visit https://www.csl.com/accessibility-statement .

descriptionByLocale.it:
Scopo della posizione: Assicurare il collegamento aziendale e affari esterni con la leadership commerciale e del sito in Svizzera. Fornire una guida strategica e una direzione ai team di affiliazione e leadership del sito sulle relazioni governative, la politica e l'advocacy, consentire l'identificazione precoce e la mitigazione dei rischi politici, e sfruttare le opportunità a sostegno delle nostre operazioni e priorità commerciali. Leader impegno con il governo a sostegno delle operazioni del sito e delle priorità commerciali, sviluppare un piano di impegno esterno a lungo termine per l'azienda.
Questo ruolo riporta a:

• Politica internazionale della testa, della difesa e degli affari governativi

• Affiliazione commerciale e gestione del sito (linea decisa)

Responsabilità e responsabilità principali:

• Sviluppare e condurre l'esecuzione di un piano strategico per guidare gli affari pubblici, anche se l'impegno di leadership che consente il successo delle operazioni di CSL, business e accesso dei pazienti alle nostre terapie in Svizzera.

• Guidare e coordinare l'impegno della società CSL con funzionari governativi, associazioni del settore, gruppi di advocacy dei pazienti e altri stakeholder. Rappresenta CSL e svolge un ruolo di primo piano nelle principali associazioni e comitati del settore. Partner con funzioni CSL per sostenere le priorità di impegno esterne in Svizzera. Partner del team Communications per promuovere relazioni strategiche sui media in Svizzera.

• Condurre lo sviluppo di aggiornamenti di politica business-relevant ai leader aziendali senior, in allineamento con le funzioni affiliate rilevanti e la leadership CEA.

• Servire in Svizzera Commercial Leadership Team, partner e collaborare pro-attivamente con i lead funzionali, tra cui Therapeutic Areas Commercial, Medical, Market Access, and Regulatory, per sviluppare ed eseguire strategie comuni.

• Servire sul team di Leadership del sito di Berna.] Guida l'impegno strategico del sito a livello politico, in collaborazione con la leadership dei siti di produzione e del team di comunicazione.

• Portare informazioni strategiche per modellare la strategia CEA in Svizzera e nella regione internazionale.

• È un partner di interfaccia chiave e un responsabile delle relazioni con i gruppi di advocacy dei pazienti, e lavora a stretto contatto con i team di Medical Affairs e Communications sul coinvolgimento del gruppo dei pazienti e sulle strategie e programmi di comunicazione aziendale in Svizzera.

Qualifiche di posizione e requisiti di esperienza:
Istruzione:

• Laureato / professionale in diritto, sanità pubblica, relazioni internazionali, scienze politiche o discipline simili preferito.

Esperienza in Svizzera:

• Minimo 8 anni di esperienza nella politica sanitaria / affari pubblici, accesso o campi comparabili

• La progettazione e i principali sforzi per costruire il profilo e l'impatto dell'azienda con importanti attori del settore sanitario a livello nazionale e locale

• Esperienza di collaborazione con colleghi a più livelli dell'organizzazione (matrix) per allineare ed eseguire obiettivi condivisi

• Forte comprensione dei lavori delle principali autorità governative/pubbliche e associazioni del settore sanitario

• Esperienza di partner con i gruppi di pazienti per avanzare obiettivi politici condivisi

• Forte, comprovata rete di relazioni con funzionari governativi, responsabili politici, industria, advocacy dei pazienti e altri stakeholder che sono influenti nella formulazione delle politiche

• Esperienza nelle industrie di prodotti biologici, plasma o farmaceutici preferita

• L'esperienza nelle relazioni mediatiche o nelle campagne di comunicazione integrate ha preferito

Competenze :

• Forti competenze analitiche, tra cui la capacità di individuare i rischi e di trarre connessioni tra questioni politiche complesse e impatto aziendale

• Forte capacità di comunicazione, compresa la capacità di comunicare descrizioni accurate e succinte di sviluppi politici/politici a dirigenti senior e internazionali

• Risultati orientati e crescita mentalità

• Forte abilità di squadra giocatore e capacità di lavorare in un'organizzazione matrice e orchestrare gli sforzi interfunzionali con risultati tangibili.

• Fluency tedesco e inglese richiesto. Altre lingue saranno un bene.

Informazioni su CSL Behring
CSL Behring è un leader globale di biotherapeutics guidato dalla nostra promessa di salvare vite umane. Concentrati sulle esigenze dei pazienti utilizzando le più recenti tecnologie, scopriamo, sviluppiamo e forniamo terapie innovative per le persone che vivono con condizioni di immunologia, ematologia, cardiovascolare e metabolica, respiratoria e trapianto aree terapeutiche. Utilizziamo tre piattaforme scientifiche strategiche di frazionamento del plasma, tecnologia delle proteine ricombinanti, e terapia cellulare e genica per supportare l'innovazione continua e perfezionare continuamente i modi in cui i prodotti possono affrontare bisogni medici non soddisfatti e aiutare i pazienti a condurre una vita piena.

CSL Behring opera una delle più grandi reti di raccolta plasma del mondo, CSL Plasma. La nostra società madre, CSL, con sede a Melbourne, Australia, impiega 32.000 persone, e fornisce le sue terapie salvavita per le persone in più di 100 paesi.
Per saperne di più su CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus e CSL Vifor visita https://www.csl.com/ e CSL Plasma all'indirizzo https://www.cslplasma.com/ .

I nostri vantaggi
Per ulteriori informazioni sui benefici di CSL visita Come CSL supporta il tuo benessere | CSL .

Condividi su Twitter
A CSL, Inclusione e Belonging è al centro della nostra missione e chi siamo. Esso alimenta la nostra innovazione giorno in e giorno fuori. Festeggiando le nostre differenze e creando una cultura della curiosità e dell'empatia, siamo in grado di comprendere e connetterci meglio con i nostri pazienti e donatori, di promuovere forti relazioni con i nostri stakeholder, e di sostenere una forza lavoro diversificata che muoverà la nostra azienda e l'industria nel futuro.
Per saperne di più sull'inclusione e la visita di appartenenza https://www.csl.com/careers/inclusion-and-belonging

Equal Opportunity Employer
CSL è un Equal Opportunity Employer. Se sei un individuo con disabilità e hai bisogno di un alloggio ragionevole per qualsiasi parte del processo di applicazione, visita https://www.csl.com/accesssibili-statement .

Positionszweck: Sicherstellung der Verbindung zwischen Corporate & External Affairs und der Geschäfts- und Standortleitung in der Schweiz. Bieten Sie den Affiliate- und Site-Führungsteams strategische Beratung und Orientierung in Bezug auf Regierungsbeziehungen, Politik und Interessenvertretung, ermöglichen Sie die frühzeitige Identifizierung und Minderung von politischen Risiken und nutzen Sie Chancen zur Unterstützung unserer Operationen und kommerziellen Prioritäten. Führen Sie die Zusammenarbeit mit der Regierung zur Unterstützung des Standortbetriebs und der kommerziellen Prioritäten und entwickeln Sie einen langfristigen externen Engagement-Plan für das Unternehmen.
Diese Rolle berichtet an:

• International Head Policy, Advocacy und Government Affairs

• Commercial Affiliate und Site Management (gepunktete Linie)

Hauptzuständigkeiten und Verantwortlichkeiten:

• Entwicklung und Leitung der Umsetzung eines strategischen Plans zur Förderung der öffentlichen Angelegenheiten, des Engagements von Führungskräften, das den Erfolg der Geschäftstätigkeit, des Geschäfts und des Patientenzugangs zu unseren Therapien in der Schweiz ermöglicht.

• Führen und koordinieren Sie das Engagement von CSL-Unternehmen mit Regierungsvertretern, Branchenverbänden, Patientenvertretungsgruppen und anderen Interessengruppen. Repräsentiert CSL und nimmt eine führende Rolle in wichtigen Branchenverbänden und -ausschüssen ein. Partner von CSL unterstützen externe Engagement-Prioritäten in der Schweiz. Zusammenarbeit mit dem Kommunikationsteam zur Förderung strategischer Medienbeziehungen in der Schweiz.

• Führen Sie die Entwicklung von geschäftsrelevanten Richtlinienaktualisierungen für leitende Unternehmensleiter in Übereinstimmung mit relevanten Affiliate-Funktionen und der CEA-Führung.

• Beauftragen Sie das Swiss Commercial Leadership Team, kooperieren Sie und arbeiten Sie proaktiv mit funktionellen Leads zusammen, einschließlich der Therapeutic Areas Commercial, Medical, Market Access und Regulatory, um gemeinsame Strategien zu entwickeln und umzusetzen.

• Dienen Sie im Berner Site Leadership Team. Förderung des strategischen Standortengagements auf politischer Ebene in Partnerschaft mit der Führung der Produktionsstätten und des Kommunikationsteams.

• Bringen Sie strategische Erkenntnisse ein, um die CEA-Strategie in der Schweiz und der internationalen Region zu gestalten.

• Ist ein wichtiger Schnittstellenpartner und Beziehungsmanager für Patientenvertretungsgruppen und arbeitet eng mit Ärzte- und Kommunikationsteams an Patientengruppen-Engagement- und Unternehmenskommunikationsstrategien und -programmen in der Schweiz zusammen.

Positionsqualifikationen und Erfahrungsanforderungen:
Bildung:

• Graduierten- / Berufsabschluss in Recht, öffentliche Gesundheit, internationale Beziehungen, Politikwissenschaften oder ähnlichen Disziplinen bevorzugt.

Erfahrungen in der Schweiz:

• Mindestens 8 Jahre Erfahrung in Gesundheitspolitik / Public Affairs, Zugang oder vergleichbaren Bereichen

• Erleben Sie die Gestaltung und Leitung der Bemühungen, das Unternehmensprofil und die Wirkung mit wichtigen Akteuren im Gesundheitswesen auf nationaler und lokaler Ebene aufzubauen

• Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit Kollegen auf mehreren Ebenen der Organisation (Matrix) zur Ausrichtung und Umsetzung gemeinsamer Ziele

• Starkes Verständnis der Arbeit von großen Regierungen / Behörden und Verbänden der Gesundheitsbranche

• Erfahrung in der Partnerschaft mit Patientengruppen zur Förderung gemeinsamer politischer Ziele

• Starkes, bewährtes Netzwerk von Beziehungen zu Regierungsbeamten, politischen Entscheidungsträgern, der Industrie, der Patientenvertretung und anderen Interessengruppen, die in der Politikgestaltung einflussreich sind

• Erfahrung in der Biologika-, Plasma- oder Pharmaindustrie bevorzugt

• Erfahrung in Media Relations oder integrierten Kommunikationskampagnen bevorzugt

Kompetenzen :

• Starke analytische Fähigkeiten, einschließlich der Fähigkeit, Risiken zu erkennen und Verbindungen zwischen komplexen politischen Themen und Geschäftsauswirkungen zu ziehen

• Starke Kommunikationsfähigkeiten, einschließlich der Fähigkeit, genaue, prägnante Beschreibungen politischer / politischer Entwicklungen an leitende Unternehmen und internationale Führungskräfte zu kommunizieren

• Ergebnisorientiert & Growth Mindset

• Starke Teamplayer-Fähigkeiten und die Fähigkeit, in einer Matrixorganisation zu arbeiten und funktionsübergreifende Bemühungen mit greifbaren Ergebnissen zu orchestrieren.

• Deutsch und Englisch fließend erforderlich. Andere Sprachen werden ein Gewinn sein.

Über CSL Behring
CSL Behring ist ein weltweit führender Anbieter von Biotherapeutika, angetrieben von unserem Versprechen, Leben zu retten. Mit dem Fokus auf die Bedürfnisse der Patienten durch den Einsatz der neuesten Technologien, entdecken, entwickeln und liefern wir innovative Therapien für Menschen mit Erkrankungen in den Bereichen Immunologie, Hämatologie, Herz-Kreislauf und Stoffwechsel, Atmung und Transplantation. Wir nutzen drei strategische wissenschaftliche Plattformen der Plasmafraktionierung, der rekombinanten Proteintechnologie sowie der Zell- und Gentherapie, um kontinuierliche Innovationen zu unterstützen und kontinuierlich Wege zu verfeinern, wie Produkte ungedeckte medizinische Bedürfnisse erfüllen und Patienten helfen können, ein volles Leben zu führen.

CSL Behring betreibt eines der weltweit größten Plasmasammelnetze, CSL Plasma. Unsere Muttergesellschaft CSL mit Hauptsitz in Melbourne, Australien, beschäftigt 32.000 Mitarbeiter und liefert ihre lebensrettenden Therapien an Menschen in mehr als 100 Ländern.
Mehr über CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus und CSL Vifor erfahren Sie unter https://www.csl.com/ und CSL Plasma unter https://www.cslplasma.com/ .

Unsere Vorteile
Weitere Informationen zu den CSL-Vorteilen finden Sie unter Wie CSL Ihr Wohlbefinden unterstützt | CSL .

Sie gehören zu CSL
Bei CSL steht Inklusion und Zugehörigkeit im Mittelpunkt unserer Mission und wer wir sind. Es treibt unsere Innovation Tag für Tag an. Indem wir unsere Unterschiede feiern und eine Kultur der Neugier und Empathie schaffen, sind wir in der Lage, unsere Patienten und Spender besser zu verstehen und zu verbinden, starke Beziehungen zu unseren Stakeholdern zu pflegen und eine vielfältige Belegschaft zu erhalten, die unser Unternehmen und unsere Branche in die Zukunft führen wird.
Weitere Informationen zu Inklusion und Zugehörigkeit finden Sie unter https://www.csl.com/careers/inclusion-and-belonging

• Expérience en matière de conception et de direction des efforts visant à établir le profil et l'impact de l'entreprise avec d'importantes parties prenantes des affaires publiques des soins de santé aux niveaux national et local

• Expérience de collaboration avec des collègues à plusieurs niveaux de l'organisation (matrice) pour s'aligner sur les objectifs communs et les réaliser

• Une bonne compréhension du fonctionnement des principaux pouvoirs publics et associations du secteur de la santé

• Expérience de partenariat avec des groupes de patients pour promouvoir des objectifs stratégiques communs

• Résultats & état d'esprit de croissance

• Maîtrise allemande et anglaise requise. D'autres langues seront un atout.

À propos de CSL Behring

Senior EHS Expert – Risk Management & Technical Safety (f/m/d)

Ihre Mission

Als Senior EHS Expert – Risk Management & Technical Safety übernehmen Sie die fachliche Verantwortung für das Risikomanagement und die technische Sicherheit am Standort Bern.

Sie fungieren als Subject Matter Expert (SME) für Risk Management, Technical Safety und Incident Investigation und begleiten technische Projekte über den gesamten Lebenszyklus. Dabei arbeiten Sie eng mit Engineering, Operations, Quality und EHS zusammen und treiben die kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung der Sicherheitsstandards am Standort voran.

Ein wesentlicher Bestandteil der Rolle ist die fachliche Unterstützung und Weiterentwicklung von EHS-Fachspezialist:innen sowie die Beratung von Führungskräften und Projektteams.

Bitte bewerben Sie sich insbesondere dann, wenn Sie Risikoanalysen (z. B. HAZOP, Bow Tie oder FMEA), Incident Investigations oder Technical-Safety-Bewertungen bereits selbstständig moderiert und durchgeführt haben sowie Erfahrung in der fachlichen Entwicklung und Begleitung anderer Fachpersonen mitbringen.

Dies ist keine klassische EHS-Generalistenrolle. Wir suchen eine Persönlichkeit mit fundierter Erfahrung in Technical Safety, Risikomanagement und der Moderation komplexer Risikoanalysen.

Risk Management & Hazard Analysis

• Moderation und Durchführung von Risikoanalysen und Gefährdungsbeurteilungen (HAZOP, Bow Tie, FMEA, JSA)

• Aufbau und Weiterentwicklung des standortweiten Risk Registers

• Entwicklung von Risikominderungsstrategien für Prozesse, Anlagen und Tätigkeiten

• Sicherstellung einer konsistenten Vorgehensweise gemäss ISO 45001 und CSL Technical Standards

Technical Safety & Incident Investigation

• Durchführung technischer Sicherheitsbewertungen

• Leitung von pSIF-Untersuchungen und Root-Cause-Analysen (ICAM, TapRooT®, RCA)

• Definition und Nachverfolgung nachhaltiger Präventionsmassnahmen

• Überführung von Lessons Learned in Standards, SOPs und Trainings

Engineering & Projekte

• EHS-Begleitung von Bau-, Modernisierungs- und Anlagenprojekten

• Teilnahme an Design Reviews, HAZOPs, PSSR, Change Controls und technischen Abnahmen

• Sicherstellung der Einhaltung globaler Technical Standards

• Moderation von Workshops und risikobasierten Entscheidungsprozessen

• Förderung einer nachhaltigen Sicherheits- und Risikokultur

• Sicherstellung der Einhaltung von ISO 45001, Schweizer Gesetzgebung und CSL Standards

• Weiterentwicklung von Prozessen, Standards und Arbeitsanweisungen

• Unterstützung bei Audits, Inspektionen und Behördenkontakten

Erfahrung

• 5 bis 8 Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung in Technical Safety, Process Safety, Risk Engineering oder EHS in einem technisch anspruchsvollen Umfeld

• Erfahrung in Incident Investigations und Root-Cause-Methoden

• Erfahrung in der Begleitung technischer Projekte

• Erfahrung im Coaching, Mentoring oder der fachlichen Anleitung von Fachpersonen

• Studium in Sicherheitstechnik, Ingenieurwesen, Chemie, Verfahrenstechnik, Umweltwissenschaften oder vergleichbarer Fachrichtung

• ISO 45001

CSL is expanding its external innovation capability, and we're looking for a Senior Director of Search & Evaluation to help shape the future of our Immunology portfolio.

We are seeking a Senior Director of Search & Evaluation to lead strategic sourcing and evaluation of later-stage external clinical assets in Immunology . This leader will focus on opportunities from Phase 2 through marketed drugs, requiring deep clinical expertise, strong engagement with external Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) and clinical investigators, and a keen understanding of evolving standards of care. The role is critical to shaping our portfolio through high-impact partnerships and transactions.

To be hybrid-based onsite (3 days a week) at one of our R&D hub sites: Zurich (CH), Maidenhead (UK), Waltham (US), King of Prussia (US). This position cannot be held remotely

Main Responsibilities & Accountabilities ​

• Serve as the senior S&E leader within the Therapy Area Leadership Team, influencing therapeutic strategy and integrating late-stage external innovation priorities into portfolio planning.​

• Lead proactive sourcing efforts for Phase 2 to marketed assets, identifying opportunities that align with TA strategy and unmet medical needs.​

• Co-lead internal meetings (with Early Search Lead) focused on evaluating and prioritizing New Product Opportunities (NPOs) within Immunology. NPO meetings are strategic checkpoints where cross-functional teams review potential assets identified by Search and decide whether to advance them for further due diligence and deal negotiations​.

• Engage extensively with external KOLs, clinical investigators, and networks to validate asset potential, understand trial designs & clinical endpoints, and anticipate competitive dynamics.​

• Maintain deep awareness of changing standards of care and competitive landscapes to inform sourcing priorities and deal strategy.​

• Drive cross-functional due diligence for late-stage assets, coordinating clinical, regulatory, commercial, and market access assessments to support governance decisions.​

• Partner closely with BD and Regional Ecosystem Leads to advance high-priority opportunities through negotiation and deal close, ensuring seamless handoff and execution​

• Represent the TA externally, leading sourcing activities at specialized conferences and building relationships with pharma, biotech, and clinical communities.​

Qualifications & Experience Requirements ​

• 15+ years in biopharma with significant experience in clinical development, external innovation, or business development.​

• Advanced degree required (MD, PhD, or equivalent).​

• Deep clinical expertise in Immunology

• Proven track record of sourcing and closing late-stage deals and engaging with KOLs and clinical networks.​

• Strong understanding of regulatory pathways, market access, and competitive standards of care.​

About CSL Behring
CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients’ needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.

CSL Behring operates one of the world’s largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries.

Our Benefits

You Belong at CSL

• Ph.D., M.Sc., or equivalent degree in Pharmacometrics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Pharmacology, Biomedical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Systems Biology, or a related discipline.

CSL’s world-class R&D organisation continues to evolve as a biotechnology leader by advancing high-quality science and technology across five therapeutic areas being Immunoglobulins, Haematology, Cardiovascular & Renal, Transplant & Immunology and Vaccines that will make a meaningful difference to the lives of patients with rare and serious diseases.

CSL is now seeking two Associate Director level scientists to design and oversee analytical strategies that support product development and lifecycle management (LCM).

The Associate Director Analytical Strategy ensures the deployment of robust, compliant, and innovative analytical approaches across pre-clinical and clinical development as well as LCM for commercial products.

These are key senior scientific and strategic leadership roles supporting a diverse portfolio of recombinant protein and gene therapy products from early development, through licensure and ongoing commercial operations.

These positions have global reach and could be based at either of our sites in Bern, Marburg, King of Prussia, Waltham or Melbourne.

Key Responsibilities

Specific responsibilities for both these roles will include:

• Developing global analytical strategies for assigned products aligned with program and corporate goals

• Provide scientific and regulatory guidance for analytical plans across all product development and LCM phasesDrive innovation in analytical technologies, platforms, and workflows

• Reviewing analytical study designs, reports, and regulatory documentation.

• Oversee development, validation, characterisation and implementation of analytical methods.

• Ensure high-quality data generation for product development and LCM programs.

• Troubleshoot complex scientific and technical challenges.

• Ensure compliance with global regulatory guidelines (FDA, EMA, ICH, GMP) and interface with regulatory agencies, responding to health authority queries.

• Lead analytical sections of regulatory submissions (IND, CTA, NDA, BLA, MAA)

• Maintaining inspection readiness and quality standards.

• Partnering with internal stakeholders across Manufacturing, Quality Control, Quality Assurance, Research and external partners such as CROs/CDMOs, academic collaborators and technology vendors.

Your Profile

• PhD in Analytical Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biochemistry, or related field (or MSc with extensive experience)

• Typically, 8+ years in bioanalysis within biotech, pharma, or CRO/CDMO environments

• Deep expertise in analytical development, product specification testing, characterisation, and data analysis.

• Demonstrated knowledge of regulatory requirements and analytical validation standards.

• Proven leadership and strategic program experience ideally in a global matrix environment.

• Experience supporting regulatory submissions and health authority interactions.

• Excellent communication skills including presenting complex information to non-scientific stakeholders.

• Experience with gene therapy products desirable, but not essential

If you want to join a team that is working every day knowing that people’s lives depend on it, then apply now.

About CSL Behring
CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients’ needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.

CSL Behring operates one of the world’s largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries.

The Senior Manager Global Regulatory Affairs CMC - Biological & Non-Biol. Products is responsible for:

Partnering closely with CSL’s R&D, Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory Affairs stakeholders to address regulatory strategy challenges and deliver innovative, timely regulatory solutions that meet evolving CMC regulatory and compliance requirements for the assigned product portfolio.

Defining global regulatory strategies, objectives, and policies that advance and support the development, registration, and lifecycle management of CSL’s biological & non-biol. products.

Represent CSL in official regulatory CMC capacities, acting as an authorized official or responsible person in interactions with regulatory agencies.

This role promotes strong cross-functional collaboration and effective communication across Global Operations, R&D, Global Regulatory Affairs, and other relevant CSL business functions to drive alignment and support CSL’s strategic business objectives.

Main 
• Responsibilities and Accountabilities

Lead the global regulatory CMC strategy across the assigned development and commercial biological & non-biol. product portfolio, collaborating closely with cross-functional leaders in Global Regulatory Affairs CMC, Global Regulatory Affairs, R&D, Quality, Global Operations, and other business functions.

Manage the development and submission of high-quality, compliant CMC regulatory submissions and submission components, including new marketing applications, clinical trial applications, variations/supplements, periodic compliance reports and renewals. Ensure timely execution aligned with regulatory expectations and business goals.

Ensure accurate and timely change control assessments of change control notifications in CSL’s quality management system for biological & non-biol. product-related change controls. This includes the country-specific reporting category and detailed submission documentation requirements.

Leverage external insights to refine strategies and implement innovative regulatory approaches that enhance CSL’s competitive positioning for its biological & non-biol. product portfolio.

Represent CSL in official regulatory CMC capacities, acting as an authorized official or responsible person in interactions with regulatory agencies. Maintain strong, positive relationships with regulators and ensure timely responses to inquiries and requests. Facilitate timely decision-making and guidance from health authorities through effective communication and relationship management.

Develop strategic and tactical plans for Global Regulatory Affairs CMC, advising Global Regulatory Affairs CMC leadership and CSL stakeholders on regulatory requirements and their implications for project timelines, compliance, and business strategy. Contribute to the evaluation of new business opportunities in collaboration with development teams.

Provide regulatory consultation to internal CSL functions, including Global Operation functions, R&D, and IT, to support the design and implementation of business processes that ensure regulatory compliance and operational excellence.

Provides tactical and strategic regulatory input and guidance, including active participation in problem solving analysis by assessing and proposing alternative solutions to issues and prepare contingency plans while still meeting regulations.

Maintains an ongoing and interactive relationship with regional and local regulatory teams to assure that all aspects of the company’s regulatory activities are conducted in full compliance with applicable regulations and at the highest level of ethical standards.

Ensure regulatory policies and procedures are developed and implemented in accordance with applicable international standards and requirements.

Support the creation and execution of regulatory policies, processes, and SOPs that meet global regulatory requirements while driving operational efficiency and effectiveness across Global Operations and its stakeholder network.

Support the outsourcing of regulatory activities, including submission quality assurance, to ensure timely and compliant delivery of services aligned with business and regulatory requirements.

Position 
• Qualifications and Experience 
• Requirements

Education & Experience

A bachelor’s degree in biological or chemical sciences, or a related field is required; an advanced degree (e.g., MS, PhD) is strongly preferred.

Over 5 years of progressive experience in regulatory roles within the biologics or plasma industry, demonstrating increasing levels of responsibility.

Strong technical foundation with in-depth knowledge of global regulations and international standards governing drug product development, manufacture, registrations, and life-cycle management.

Proven expertise in authoring, reviewing, and managing regulatory submissions ensuring accuracy, compliance, and timely delivery.

Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and collaborate effectively with key stakeholders.

Skilled in motivating, mentoring, and guiding diverse teams within a matrixed organizational structure, fostering a culture of accountability and excellence.

Exceptional oral and written communication skills, with a strong ability to negotiate, influence, and represent regulatory positions effectively.

Committed to the highest standards of compliance, integrity, and adaptability, with a strong focus on aligning regulatory strategy with evolving business needs.

Ability to use precedent and previous experience to develop innovative and flexible approaches to achieve goals.

Competencies

Ensures Accountability: Follows through on commitments and makes sure others do the same; Acts with a clear sense of ownership; Takes personal responsibility for decisions, actions, and failures; Establishes clear responsibilities and processes for monitoring work and measuring results; Designs feedback loops into work.

Drives Results: Has a strong bottom-line orientation; Persists in accomplishing objectives despite obstacles and setbacks; Has a track record of exceeding goals successfully; Pushes self and helps others achieve results.

Drives Vision & Purpose: Talks about future possibilities in a positive way; Creates milestones and symbols to rally support behind the vision; Articulates the vision in a way everyone can relate to; Creates organization-wide energy and optimism for the future; Shows personal commitment to the vision.

Instills Trust: Follows through on commitments; Is seen as direct and truthful; Keeps confidences; Practices what he/she preaches; Shows consistent between words and actions.

Communicates Effectively: Is effective in a variety of communication settings: one-on-one, small and large groups, among diverse styles and position levels, with internal and external stakeholders/audiences. Attentively listens to others; Adjusts to fit the audience and the message; Provides timely and helpful information to others across the organization; Encourages the open expression of diverse ideas and opinions.

Builds Effective Teams: Establishes common objectives and a shared mindset; Creates a feelings of belonging and strong team morale; Shares wins and rewards team efforts; Fosters open dialogue and collaboration among the team.

Drives Engagement: Structures the work so it aligns with people's goals and motivators; Empowers others; Makes each person feel his/her contributions are important; Invites input and shares ownership and visibility; Shows a clear connection between people's motivators and the organizational goals.

Manages Ambiguity: Deals comfortably with the uncertainty of change; Effectively handles risk; Can decide and act without the total picture; Is calm and productive, even when things are up in the air; Deals constructively with problems that do not have clear solutions or outcomes.

Collaborates: Works cooperatively with others across the site, matrix, network and enterprise to achieve shared objectives; Represents own interests while being fair to others and their areas; Partners with others to get work done; Credits others for their contributions and accomplishments; Gains trust and support of others.

Decision Quality: Makes sound decisions, even in the absence of complete information; Relies on a mixture of analysis, wisdom, experience, and judgment when making decisions; Considers all relevant factors and uses appropriate decision-making criteria and principles; Recognizes when a quick 80% solution will suffice.

Global Perspective: Looks toward the broadest possible view of an issue or challenge; Thinks and talks in global and network terms; Understands the position of the organization within a global, network and enterprise context; Knows the impact of global trends on the organization.

Being Resilient: Is confident under pressure; Handles and manages crises effectively; Maintains a positive attitude despite adversity; Bounces back from setbacks; Grows from hardships and negative experiences.

jobs.description:
The Regional Regulatory Lead (RRL) is responsible for both strategic and operational regulatory activities within the assigned Therapeutic Area (TA) for designated products across designated regions or sub-regions: Asia Pacific (APAC), Latin America (LATAM), Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Adriatics, Middle East & Africa (MEA) and Partner Business. The RPL can be based at either of the following sites: Zurich (Switzerland), or Maidenhead (UK).

Working with the Therapeutic Area Lead and the Global Regulatory Lead, the RRL contributes to global regulatory strategy and manages regional regulatory strategies that align with commercial and business priorities.

This position ensures adherence to regional regulatory requirements and oversees submissions related to marketing applications, life cycle management, tender applications, interactions with Health Authorities, PSURs, and associated reporting responsibilities. The RRL partners with Local Regulatory Representative (LRR), Regulatory Partner Representative (RPR), and other internal stakeholders to facilitate timely Health Authority approvals.

Key Responsibilities

• Serve as the regional regulatory strategist for the assigned product portfolio and countries in alignment with the global strategy and priorities across designated regions or sub-regions: Asia Pacific (APAC), Latin America (LATAM), Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Adriatics, Middle East & Africa (MEA) and Partner Business.

• Develop and implement regulatory strategies that meet regional requirements for any regulatory activities, while identifying the most efficient approval pathways by leveraging LRR or RPR local inputs.

• Contribute to RST activities and support the development of Global Regulatory Strategy, including planning and preparation of projects or response for complex scientific questions that require product expertise and cross-functional collaboration.

• Lead the strategic oversight of regulatory activities across the assigned product portfolio and countries to drive optimal Health Authority outcomes and proactively anticipate and manage emerging regulatory risks.

• Provide strategic oversight to ensure high-quality regulatory submission documentation for all regulatory activities, including responses to Health Authority questions, aligned with schedules and regional requirements, while fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

• Build and maintain strong collaboration with Local Regulatory Representatives (LRR), Regulatory Partner Representatives (RPR), and other internal stakeholders.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with regional Health Authorities by delivering high quality, compliant regulatory documentation and engaging with clarity and influence to support positive outcomes for CSL.

• Stay current with international legislation and guidelines relevant to any CSL products and other key related CSL activities and initiatives (e.g. rare diseases, orphan drugs, toll manufacturing, reliance pathways)

• Act as a subject matter expert by assessing the impact of local or regional regulation and identifying potential regulatory risks.

• Contribute to continuous process improvements to enhance regulatory execution, compliance, and operational excellence.

Your Profile

• A degree in Biological or Medical Science or Pharmacy, preferably with a post-graduate qualification. Degree e.g. in Drug Regulatory Affairs advantageous

• At least 5 years of regulatory experience within the international markets, supported by additional pharmaceutical /industry experience.

• English mandatory, and additional language is an asset (e.g. Arabic, French, Spanish, Russian)

• Understanding of the scientific principles and technical requirements relevant to the development of a pharmaceutical product and understanding of the principles of GMP, GCP.

Why Join Us?
This is a unique opportunity to contribute to the delivery of life-changing therapies to patients worldwide while working within a collaborative and innovative global environment.

At CSL, we are committed to continuous improvement, scientific excellence, and making a meaningful difference in patients’ lives.

We are looking forward to receiving your online application. Applications must include a motivation letter and CV.

About CSL Behring
CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients’ needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.

CSL Behring operates one of the world’s largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries.
To learn more about CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor visit https://www.csl.com/ and CSL Plasma at https://www.cslplasma.com/ .

Our Benefits
For more information on CSL benefits visit How CSL Supports Your Well-being | CSL .

You Belong at CSL
At CSL, Inclusion and Belonging is at the core of our mission and who we are. It fuels our innovation day in and day out. By celebrating our differences and creating a culture of curiosity and empathy, we are able to better understand and connect with our patients and donors, foster strong relationships with our stakeholders, and sustain a diverse workforce that will move our company and industry into the future.

The Regional Regulatory Lead (RRL) is responsible for both strategic and operational regulatory activities within the assigned Therapeutic Area (TA) for designated products across designated regions or sub-regions: Asia Pacific (APAC), Latin America (LATAM), Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Adriatics, Middle East & Africa (MEA) and Partner Business. The RPL can be based at either of the following sites: Zurich (Switzerland), or Maidenhead (UK).

Working with the Therapeutic Area Lead and the Global Regulatory Lead, the RRL contributes to global regulatory strategy and manages regional regulatory strategies that align with commercial and business priorities.

This position ensures adherence to regional regulatory requirements and oversees submissions related to marketing applications, life cycle management, tender applications, interactions with Health Authorities, PSURs, and associated reporting responsibilities. The RRL partners with Local Regulatory Representative (LRR), Regulatory Partner Representative (RPR), and other internal stakeholders to facilitate timely Health Authority approvals.

Key Responsibilities

• Serve as the regional regulatory strategist for the assigned product portfolio and countries in alignment with the global strategy and priorities across designated regions or sub-regions: Asia Pacific (APAC), Latin America (LATAM), Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Adriatics, Middle East & Africa (MEA) and Partner Business.

• Develop and implement regulatory strategies that meet regional requirements for any regulatory activities, while identifying the most efficient approval pathways by leveraging LRR or RPR local inputs.

• Contribute to RST activities and support the development of Global Regulatory Strategy, including planning and preparation of projects or response for complex scientific questions that require product expertise and cross-functional collaboration.

• Lead the strategic oversight of regulatory activities across the assigned product portfolio and countries to drive optimal Health Authority outcomes and proactively anticipate and manage emerging regulatory risks.

• Provide strategic oversight to ensure high-quality regulatory submission documentation for all regulatory activities, including responses to Health Authority questions, aligned with schedules and regional requirements, while fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

• Build and maintain strong collaboration with Local Regulatory Representatives (LRR), Regulatory Partner Representatives (RPR), and other internal stakeholders.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with regional Health Authorities by delivering high quality, compliant regulatory documentation and engaging with clarity and influence to support positive outcomes for CSL.

• Stay current with international legislation and guidelines relevant to any CSL products and other key related CSL activities and initiatives (e.g. rare diseases, orphan drugs, toll manufacturing, reliance pathways)

• Act as a subject matter expert by assessing the impact of local or regional regulation and identifying potential regulatory risks.

• Contribute to continuous process improvements to enhance regulatory execution, compliance, and operational excellence.

Your Profile

• A degree in Biological or Medical Science or Pharmacy, preferably with a post-graduate qualification. Degree e.g. in Drug Regulatory Affairs advantageous

• At least 5 years of regulatory experience within the international markets, supported by additional pharmaceutical /industry experience.

• English mandatory, and additional language is an asset (e.g. Arabic, French, Spanish, Russian)

• Understanding of the scientific principles and technical requirements relevant to the development of a pharmaceutical product and understanding of the principles of GMP, GCP.

Why Join Us?
This is a unique opportunity to contribute to the delivery of life-changing therapies to patients worldwide while working within a collaborative and innovative global environment.

At CSL, we are committed to continuous improvement, scientific excellence, and making a meaningful difference in patients’ lives.

We are looking forward to receiving your online application. Applications must include a motivation letter and CV.

About CSL Behring
CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients’ needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.

CSL Behring operates one of the world’s largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries.
To learn more about CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor visit https://www.csl.com/ and CSL Plasma at https://www.cslplasma.com/ .

Our Benefits
For more information on CSL benefits visit How CSL Supports Your Well-being | CSL .

You Belong at CSL
At CSL, Inclusion and Belonging is at the core of our mission and who we are. It fuels our innovation day in and day out. By celebrating our differences and creating a culture of curiosity and empathy, we are able to better understand and connect with our patients and donors, foster strong relationships with our stakeholders, and sustain a diverse workforce that will move our company and industry into the future.
To learn more about inclusion and belonging visit https://www.csl.com/careers/inclusion-and-belonging

Ce poste assure le respect des exigences réglementaires régionales et supervise les présentations liées aux demandes de commercialisation, à la gestion du cycle de vie, aux demandes d'appel d'offres, aux interactions avec les autorités sanitaires, aux PSUR et aux responsabilités connexes en matière de rapport. Principales responsabilités

• Servir de stratège réglementaire régional pour le portefeuille de produits assigné et les pays conformément à la stratégie et aux priorités mondiales pour les régions ou sous-régions désignées : Asie-Pacifique (APAC), Amérique latine (LATAM), Communauté d'États indépendants (CEI), Adriatique, Moyen-Orient et Afrique (MEA) et Partner Business.

• Contribuer aux activités de RST et appuyer l'élaboration d'une stratégie réglementaire mondiale, y compris la planification et la préparation de projets ou de réponses à des questions scientifiques complexes qui nécessitent une expertise des produits et une collaboration interfonctionnelle.

• Diriger la surveillance stratégique des activités de réglementation dans l'ensemble du portefeuille de produits et des pays affectés afin d'obtenir des résultats optimaux pour les autorités sanitaires et d'anticiper et de gérer de façon proactive les risques réglementaires émergents.

• Établir et maintenir une solide collaboration avec les représentants locaux de la réglementation (RRL), les représentants des partenaires de la réglementation (RPR) et d'autres intervenants internes.

• Établir et maintenir des relations solides avec les autorités régionales de la santé en fournissant une documentation réglementaire de haute qualité et conforme et en engageant des efforts de clarté et d'influence pour appuyer les résultats positifs de l'ACS.

• Restez au courant de la législation et des lignes directrices internationales applicables à tout produit de LSC et à d'autres activités et initiatives clés connexes de LSC (p. ex. maladies rares, médicaments orphelins, fabrication de péages, voies de dépendance)

• Contribuer à l'amélioration continue des processus afin d'améliorer l'exécution réglementaire, la conformité et l'excellence opérationnelle.
